portal_title: Nondimensional Staged Feedback Control of Mitochondrial Heteroplasmy Dynamics with Host-Emulated Verification on an Ultra-Low-Power RV32IMF_Zve32x Neural Processing Unit
portal_abstract: Restoring bioenergetics in cells with mutant mitochondria ($D$) alongside wild-type organelles ($W$) requires navigating nonlinear couplings among clearance bottlenecks ($B$), reactive oxygen species (ROS) conversion, and replicative selection ($k_{\mathrm{rep,adv}} \ge 1$). We formulate an eight-state ODE model unified 1-to-1 across analytical equations, FP64 simulation, and bare-metal C99 firmware to analyze staged feedback control: bottleneck clearance ($u_0$), selective mitophagy ($u_1$), and biogenesis ($u_2$) gated at heteroplasmy $h \le 0.080$ and $B \le 0.120$. Via Nagumo's subtangent theorem, we prove forward invariance of the Stage-1 safe set ($\mathrm{EP} \le 1.0456 < \theta_{\mathrm{GSH}} = 1.150$, $W_{\min} = 0.600 > 0.450$, $\lambda_{\min} = 0.01085\,\mathrm{d}^{-1}$), derive exact selection collapse $s(t) = \int_0^t \lambda_h(q)\,dq$ ($0.0000$ error), and bound constant-rate rescaling $\hat{\tau} = \hat{\lambda}_0 t$ across three non-homothetic regimes ($R^2 = 0.9828$, sup error $0.0493 \le 0.1213$). Discrete-adjoint optimal control (300 variables, gradient error $1.95 \times 10^{-9}$) shows Pontryagin trajectories ride $\mathrm{EP} = \theta_{\mathrm{GSH}}$ ($J_{\mathrm{PMP}}^* = 0.7262$ vs. threshold $J_{\mathrm{thresh}} = 0.8875$), trading $+22.21\%$ cost for a $20.1\%$ redox margin, while a $31 \times 31$ $(W_0, k_{\mathrm{dmg}})$ map separates collapse ($18.9\%$) from build-first rescue ($2.9\%$). Under 4-channel sensing ($\kappa(\mathcal{O}_7) = 745.6$), $\pm 20\%$ rate mismatch, and $6.5\sigma$ spikes, margin-tightened Huber-EKF ($\hat{h}_{\mathrm{gate}} = 0.065$) cuts premature switches from $24.17\%$ to $5.00\%$. On host-emulated Coral NPU (RV32IMF_Zve32x, 3,696 B DTCM), fixed-point Huber-EKF ($0.94\%$ RMSE) and Q16.16/Q8.24 $\Sigma\Delta$ RK4 prevent deadband stalling ($0.0534\%$-$0.0563\%$ error vs. $100\%$ naive stall).
